title: The Agent Trust Lifecycle
content: One model of Discover→Register→Evaluate→Protect→Improve→Release→Monitor; distinguish activities from registry stages Registered/Tested/Protected/Adapted.
acceptance: Mermaid and text explain the different concepts; definitions are no longer copied across guides.

title: Personas, Policies, and Evaluation Context
content: How Personas and Policies shape Harness generation and Red Team context; an evaluation Policy is not automatically a runtime Control or an RL Policy.
acceptance: One example connects context to a test; AOG and ADG link here instead of repeating Why sections.

title: Interpret Evaluation Evidence
content: Trust Score, severity, coverage, reports, and behavioral/Red Team evidence; requirements for comparing runs and why a result is not a guarantee.
acceptance: No UI clicking instructions or API syntax; the same finding links to Console and programmatic investigation guides.

title: How the Controls Engine Works
content: Step→Scope→Selector→Evaluator→Action; the relationship between VijilDome, Dome, ControlEngine, and TrustRuntime without treating them as aliases.
acceptance: A diagram and one example explain allow/deny/steer/observe; full signatures stay in P080.

title: How Trust Runtime Works
content: Identity versus Agent ID, constraints, tool MAC, attestation, audit, and heartbeats; boundaries of in-process enforcement and framework integration.
acceptance: Clearly states when identity is attested and what is outside coverage; links integration and API reference.

title: Evaluation Harness Reference
content: A versioned catalog of standard/custom/compliance/benchmark Harnesses: public ID/alias, type, availability, coverage, and output/report support.
acceptance: Every previous lookup item has a destination; the catalog does not claim all unless its source covers everything. Namespaces and short aliases are mapped explicitly.

title: Evaluation Scenario Reference
content: One catalog of Scenario IDs, descriptions, Harness membership, and old/new taxonomy mappings.
acceptance: Each entry has a visible stable ID; the domain owner resolves inconsistent legacy sections before publication.

title: Evaluation Probe Reference
content: Probe ID, test description, prompt collection, Scenarios, and Detectors; distinguish a Probe definition from an executed prompt.
acceptance: Every existing row is transferred or explicitly marked retired; prose and JSON/CSV come from the same versioned source where one exists.

title: Evaluation Detector Reference
content: Evaluation Detector IDs, inputs, results, and Probe mappings; explicitly separate from the runtime registry.
acceptance: Does not claim all evaluation Detectors live within runtime Guards; shared implementations are identified individually.

title: Evaluation Coverage by Dimension
content: Dimension→Scenario→Probe→Detector mapping replacing the three hover catalogs; Reliability, Safety, and Security sections.
acceptance: IDs are ordinary readable text in both HTML and Markdown; there are no three independently maintained copies of the full Probe catalog.

title: Agent Registration Contract
content: Fields, protocols, access levels, lifecycle/status distinctions, required values, secrets handling, and archive/delete semantics per interface.
acceptance: The supported UI/SDK/MCP/REST naming table distinguishes endpoint registration from source import and invents no equivalences.

title: Evaluation Contracts and Results
content: Scales and units; sample_size units; Harness IDs; evaluation_id/engagement_id/campaign_id; statuses and terminal outcomes; report readiness, pagination, and error contracts by mode/interface.
acceptance: The domain owner confirms differences; behavioral and Red Team examples cover success, failure, and timeout; no future endpoint is presented as available.

title: Dome Configuration Reference
content: DomeConfig, Guard/Guardrail/Detector keys, defaults, configuration sources/precedence, extras, environment variables, on-error, and the Console-supported subset.
acceptance: Every field has type/default/scope/version; the extracted installation task and how-to guides link to the canonical table.

title: Dome Results and Telemetry Reference
content: ScanResult, BatchScanResult, DomePayload, DetectionMethod protocol, framework result differences, actual metric units, and signal fields.
acceptance: Distinguishes flagged/enforced/sanitized and seconds/milliseconds; examples are checked against the release rather than legacy pseudo APIs.

title: Trust Runtime API Reference
content: secure_agent/TrustRuntime signatures, constraint schema/precedence, identity and tool decisions, manifests, audit events, heartbeats, and failure modes.
acceptance: Manifest signing/verification has a confirmed supported procedure or a clear operator prerequisite; the retired CLI reference is not reconstructed.

title: Framework Integration Reference
content: Version and support-scope matrix; callback/hook/proxy signatures, results, and blocking behavior; streaming and tool-enforcement limits.
acceptance: All five existing integrations distinguish content scanning from identity-aware enforcement; how-to examples do not maintain duplicate full tables.

title: Dome Service HTTP API Reference
content: Health/configuration/input/output/batch HTTP contracts; authentication, response schemas, Bedrock compatibility, and container telemetry settings.
acceptance: Identifies this as the Dome service API, distinct from Console REST API and Controls Python API; documented compatibility does not promise an identical Bedrock contract.

title: Platform Versions and Capability Availability
content: A small confirmed matrix of versions, deployment feature flags, preview/GA/unsupported status, public interfaces, and compatible combinations.
acceptance: Each status has a release/source owner and verification date; documentation does not infer availability from the existence of an SDK method or Pydantic model.

title: Authenticate to Vijil
content: Obtain and verify SDK/MCP credentials, team, and gateway settings; terminal helpers only where they are a supported necessity, not a third workflow.
acceptance: One successful read verifies identity and team; credential differences and refresh limits link to SDK/REST reference.

title: Connect the Vijil MCP Server
content: Connect the standalone MCP server to a client; clearly distinguish it from Claude Code plugin installation and the Dome MCP protection proxy.
acceptance: vijil_status and one read-only call work; the machine-readable description requires no CLI evaluation tab.

title: Install and Configure the Python SDK
content: Choose a confirmed Python/package version, install, authenticate, select gateway/team, and perform one read.
acceptance: All prerequisites are explicit; full credential precedence exists only in reference. Reuse an existing non-TOC file only after separately reviewing its contents.

title: Gate a Release on Evaluation Evidence
content: Python SDK CI gate: start/poll/timeout, inspect status, available score and relevant findings, retain evaluation ID/report, and set the exit code.
acceptance: failed/cancelled/degraded/missing score cannot pass; the threshold has an explicit scale and policy owner; it does not use another run's latest score.

title: Register an Agent Programmatically
content: SDK/MCP endpoint registration→verify→save Agent ID, with separate links to source import and protocol compatibility.
acceptance: The example does not treat client.register(path) as an alias for endpoint creation; the saved ID leads into evaluation.

title: Install an Endpoint Collector
content: macOS/Linux/Windows installation variants of the same task; artifacts, privileges, credentials, enrollment verification, logs, upgrades, and revocation.
acceptance: Each OS has enrollment evidence, not merely a Running service; WSL limitations and paths remain explicit. Replace bootstrap CLI only with a confirmed supported workflow.

title: Install a Network Collector
content: VM/container, routability, daemon mode, credential handoff, required capabilities, blind spots, and verification.
acceptance: The Collector remains active for Scan now; routing and credential failures lead to precise diagnostics.

title: Install a Kubernetes Collector
content: Chart/image access, cluster prerequisites, service account/RBAC, secret references, Helm installation, and enrollment confirmation.
acceptance: Secrets need not appear in inline commands/release values; supported chart/cluster versions and team/Target attribution are specified.

title: Install an AWS Cloud API Collector
content: EKS/OIDC/IAM prerequisites, chart configuration, and scan scheduling; the AWS API Collector requires no LLM key.
acceptance: Permissions and the identity model are confirmed for the release; no generic language-model key requirement is copied from other Collectors.

title: Retrieve and Investigate Red Team Evidence
content: From SDK/MCP evaluation ID to status, wave/seed artifacts, transcripts, judgments, and reports; inspect degraded outcomes and use bounded polling.
acceptance: The example uses the same confirmed ID flow as launch; reference defines enums/options, while Concepts explains evidence.

title: Prepare AWS Infrastructure for Vijil
content: VPC/EKS/RDS/S3/DNS/IAM prerequisites and the exact provisioning outcome, with clear customer/Vijil responsibilities.
acceptance: Separate from application Helm installation; copied commands do not depend on an unexplained private checkout or internal staging account.

title: Self-Hosted Configuration Reference
content: Chart values, secrets, environment variables, infrastructure/version compatibility, feature flags, optional Darwin dependency, and required resources.
acceptance: Defaults and security-sensitive examples state their scope; customer values do not use unexplained internal staging values; release version is specified.

title: Claude Code Plugin Command Reference
content: /vijil commands, arguments, prerequisites, output, weekly allowance, and side effects; clearly identify commands that only propose changes.
acceptance: Plugin commands, MCP tools, and shell commands have distinct identifiers; supported plugin commands are not removed with the CLI reference.

title: Review and Apply an Adaptation Proposal
content: Owner Console review: inspect evidence/diff, approve/reject/apply, re-evaluate, and roll back, only for a confirmed available Darwin workflow.
acceptance: Product confirms UI behavior and approve versus apply semantics; a generic model or specification endpoint is insufficient for publication.
gate: Confirm an enabled/released Darwin workflow; until then, keep this in the backlog with status described in Concepts.

title: Adapt an Agent and Validate the Proposal
content: SDK adapt→job status→proposal diff→review/apply→re-evaluate; distinguish corrective adaptation from generative evolve and application deployment.
acceptance: Job failure and proposal rejection are covered; permissions, version, and supported backend are confirmed; there is no promise that the platform automatically deploys the application.
gate: Confirm an enabled/released Darwin workflow; until then, retain only the backlog item and capability reference.
